correctness.rationale: Graph vertices and all 30 edges are explicit. Lemma 2.2 identifies every scale-three Čech facet as an edge-neighborhood union. Exhaustive enumeration verifies 30 facets, 1170 faces, 4160 Hasse incidences, and a complete 578-pair acyclic matching with critical cells in dimensions 0, 2, 3 of respective counts 1,1,12. Exact signed integral algebraic Morse reductions show the entire differential from critical 3-cells to critical 2-cell is zero. The resulting one-point CW complex has a 2-sphere two-skeleton and twelve nullhomotopically attached 3-cells, giving the asserted wedge. Separate mod-2 and mod-3 ranks (19,131,248,150,30) and Euler -10 corroborate homology, but the Morse and attaching-map argument—not finite experiments alone—establishes homotopy.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral graph is the canonical twenty-vertex Platonic cubic graph of girth five; scale three is the first integer above the strict Čech graph-recovery range r<5/2. The exact integral homotopy type is mixed-dimensional (one 2-sphere and twelve 3-spheres), establishes failure of shellability for its pure 5-complex, and distinguishes an intrinsically motivated threshold from previously tabulated single-neighborhood/even-scale complexes. This natural first-threshold structural classification is mathematically informative beyond numerical homology or a routine reparameterization.
